title: Move money atomically
summary: Wrap a transfer in a transaction, then reason about isolation and recovery.

scenario.briefing: A transfer debits one account and credits another. The current script applies only the debit. Make the pair atomic, then choose the isolation behavior the report needs.

objectives.description: Apply both balance changes inside one transaction.
Identify a read anomaly from its observed behavior.
Explain transactions, isolation, and recovery accurately.

hints: Both updates must be inside one unit of work.
Start with BEGIN IMMEDIATE and finish with COMMIT.
Debit a1 and credit a2 by the same amount.
BEGIN IMMEDIATE; UPDATE accounts SET balance_cents = balance_cents - 2500 WHERE id = 'a1'; UPDATE accounts SET balance_cents = balance_cents + 2500 WHERE id = 'a2'; COMMIT;

misconceptions.description: Applying the debit without the matching credit.
misconceptions.feedback: The seed has equal balances. After the transfer a1 must be 2500 lower and a2 2500 higher in the same committed unit.

misconceptions.description: Confusing a dirty read with a non-repeatable read.
misconceptions.feedback: A dirty read sees uncommitted data. Here the second read sees a different committed value, which is a non-repeatable read.

misconceptions.description: Believing each statement commits immediately inside a transaction.
misconceptions.feedback: Inside an explicit transaction, changes become durable at COMMIT or disappear at ROLLBACK.

misconceptions.description: Believing a recent backup removes the need for transactions.
misconceptions.feedback: A backup restores a past state. It cannot make a multi-statement change atomic while the system is running.

sections.title: A transaction is one unit of change
sections.body: A transaction groups statements so the database applies all of them or none of them. BEGIN opens the unit, COMMIT makes the changes durable, and ROLLBACK discards them. A debit without its matching credit is not a completed transfer.

sections.title: Isolation describes concurrent visibility
sections.body: READ COMMITTED lets a statement see changes committed by other transactions. REPEATABLE READ keeps a stable snapshot for the transaction. SERIALIZABLE prevents the schedules that produce phantom reads. Higher isolation reduces concurrency, so choose it from the anomalies the application can tolerate.

sections.title: Backups are recovery, not isolation
sections.body: A backup or point-in-time recovery protects against lost storage and operator mistakes. It does not make a multi-statement transfer atomic. Test restores regularly, and keep the backup outside the failure domain of the primary database.

vocabulary.definition: A group of statements that commits or rolls back as one unit.
The rules for which concurrent changes a transaction can observe.
A durable record of changes used for recovery and replication.
Restoring a database to a chosen moment using backups and logs.

steps.title: Make the transfer atomic
steps.prompt: Edit transfer.sql. Move 2500 cents from a1 to a2 inside one transaction so both balances change or neither does.

files.content: UPDATE accounts SET balance_cents = balance_cents - 2500 WHERE id = 'a1';

tests.verify: SELECT id, balance_cents FROM accounts ORDER BY id;

hints: The debit and credit are two statements that must travel together.
Open the transaction before the first update.
Commit only after both updates succeed.
Use BEGIN IMMEDIATE, both UPDATE statements, then COMMIT.

database.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE accounts (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, balance_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (balance_cents >= 0));

steps.title: Name the anomaly
steps.prompt: A report reads the same row twice inside one transaction and sees a different committed value. Which anomaly is this?

quiz.explanation: A non-repeatable read sees a row change between two reads in the same transaction. A phantom read sees new rows appear for the same predicate.

hints: The same row is read twice and changes.
A dirty read would require uncommitted data.
A phantom read is about new rows matching a predicate.

steps.title: Transactions, isolation, and backups

statements.label: A transaction needs an explicit COMMIT or ROLLBACK boundary.
Every statement commits immediately inside an explicit transaction.
READ COMMITTED can see changes committed by other transactions between statements.
A recent backup removes the need for transactions.

steps.explanation: Transactions define atomicity. Isolation levels define visibility. Backups provide recovery but do not replace either guarantee.
hints: An explicit transaction ends at COMMIT or ROLLBACK.
READ COMMITTED takes a fresh snapshot for each statement.
